claim: L-Mul approximates floating-point multiplication with integer addition, reducing the mantissa operation from O(m^2) complexity to O(m).
stance_target: L-Mul is a genuinely novel, low-complexity approximate-multiplication algorithm suitable for hardware realization
scope_conditions: floating-point multiplication of numbers with m-bit mantissas
quoted_support: We propose L-Mul, a FP multiplication algorithm with O(n) complexity, where n is the bit size of its FP operands... We remove this operation and introduce a new multiplication algorithm that processes mantissas with a computational complexity of O(m).

claim: Applying L-Mul in tensor processing hardware can theoretically reduce energy cost by 95% for element-wise floating-point tensor multiplication and 80% for dot products, based on Horowitz (2014) energy figures where fp32 multiplication costs 37x the energy of int32 addition.
stance_target: approximate arithmetic replacing multiplication with addition yields large, quantifiable energy savings -- the core motivation cited by downstream FPGA hardware papers
scope_conditions: tensor processing hardware, fp32/fp16 accumulation precision assumptions
quoted_support: applying the L-Mul operation in tensor processing hardware can potentially reduce 95% energy cost by element-wise floating point tensor multiplications and 80% energy cost of dot products.
numbers: 37x energy cost fp32 mult vs int32 add
4x energy cost fp32 mult vs fp32 add

claim: L-Mul with a 4-bit mantissa achieves comparable numerical precision to float8 e4m3 multiplication, and L-Mul with a 3-bit mantissa outperforms float8 e5m2 multiplication.
stance_target: L-Mul can substitute for FP8 multiplication with equal or better precision at lower hardware cost -- the direct justification for building an FP8 L-Mul multiplier in hardware
scope_conditions: theoretical error estimation and numerical analysis experiments across textual, visual, symbolic tasks
quoted_support: L-Mul with 4-bit mantissa achieves comparable precision as float8 e4m3 multiplications, and L-Mul with 3-bit mantissa outperforms float8 e5m2.

claim: Replacing standard multiplication with L-Mul in the attention mechanism of pretrained transformer LLMs (no additional training) causes only 0.07% average performance loss on language reasoning benchmarks and a 0.12% accuracy gain on vision tasks.
stance_target: L-Mul is near-lossless when substituted into real, deployed LLM/vision-transformer pipelines without retraining
scope_conditions: training-free substitution into pretrained transformer models, commonsense/structured-reasoning/language-understanding and visual QA/object-hallucination/instruction-following benchmarks
quoted_support: the average performance loss of L-Mul-based attention is 0.07% across commonsense, structured reasoning, language understanding. On vision tasks, L-Mul-based attention gained 0.12% accuracy improvement on visual question answering, object hallucination, and free-form visual instruction tasks.

claim: GPUs cannot fully exploit the L-Mul algorithm's efficiency because they lack native hardware support, motivating dedicated hardware/FPGA implementations.
stance_target: L-Mul's benefits require purpose-built digital hardware (e.g., FPGA), directly motivating a hardware-implementation research/student project rather than a software-only replication
scope_conditions: Nvidia GPU simulation of L-Mul via inline PTX assembly
quoted_support: Due to the absence of native implementation, GPUs cannot fully exploit the efficiency of the L-Mul algorithm. We recommend training and hosting L-Mul-based models on devices integrated with specialized architectural designs.
